source.title: Scaling Laws of Synthetic Data for Language Models
source.authors: Zeyu Qin; Qing-Xiu Dong; Xingxing Zhang; Li Dong; Xiao-Long Huang; Ziyi Yang; Mahmoud Khademi; Dong-Dong Zhang; H. Awadalla; Yi R. Fung; Weizhu Chen; Minhao Cheng; Fu-Ru Wei

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling behavior in a new training setting: supervised fine-tuning with synthetic data, using downstream benchmark error rates rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study reports synthetic-data scaling curves, fitted decay exponents, and validation predictions. It also compares two scaling-curve formulations. Comparisons of synthetic-data generation methods and their downstream scores are not rows unless they report the scaling behavior itself. Future Table 1 projections are not rows because they are extrapolations without measured outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study fits scaling curves of downstream MATH error against synthetic SFT data size for 1B, 3B and 8B Llama models. It checks fitted predictions at a held-out larger size and compares a pure power-law (marginal) form with a rectified form. This bears on V5 (fine-tuning regime), V6 (downstream predictability) and V7 (functional-form dependence). It does not measure pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that synthetic math data from SynthLLM follows a rectified scaling law across model sizes, allowing accurate prediction when doubling data size. From extrapolated (unverified) projections, they add that gains diminish near 300B tokens and larger models approach their ceiling with fewer tokens (8B about 1T, 3B about 4T). They also say the Dl term is needed because base models already have math ability from pretraining.
record.recipe_differences: Uses continued SFT on synthetic math data and downstream benchmark error rates, rather than pretraining runs measured by held-out cross-entropy; tests rectified scaling rather than parameter-token-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The chosen scaling formulation matters: the marginal form fits and predicts poorly, while the rectified form works effectively. The reported fitted β also differs by model size, with the 1B value smaller than those for the larger models.
record.problems: The study measures downstream benchmark error rates, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. The scaling experiment focuses mainly on math and synthetic-data SFT. The paper gives limited numerical detail for the fitted curves and reports no uncertainty estimates. Its discussion refers to a 7B model although the experimental setup lists an 8B model.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's projected accuracies from 10B to 4T synthetic tokens were omitted because they are unverified extrapolations, not measured outcomes. Other dataset-method and benchmark comparisons were omitted because they do not report the scaling behavior itself.

untested.parts: Pretraining held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
Not tested as stated. Validation is about a 2x extrapolation on downstream error, not loss over orders of magnitude. Table 1 projections to 4T tokens are unverified.
Only math SFT on synthetic data is tested. There is no scaling curve for coding (single-point results only), and no other modalities, repeated-data pretraining or transfer.
Downstream performance against pretraining loss is not tested, and scaling across model size is not fitted jointly. Only MATH is used for curve fitting.
No comparison of exponents across published laws, parameter counting, schedules or fitting methods beyond the two functional forms.

missing.what: Accuracy versus number of generated questions per document (50K–300K samples) for Level-2/3 versus rephrase/persona augmentation on Llama-3.1-8B. The augmentation methods saturate while Level-2/3 keep improving: data-generation method changes the scaling behaviour.
Fitted ratio B/Dl (lowest, 56.3, for the 8B/'7B' model), which the authors tie to initial capability. No other fitted parameter values are given numerically.

record.verdict_notes: Predictions are validated only about 2x beyond the fitted range and only by figure. No uncertainty or goodness-of-fit numbers are reported. The paper's 7B/8B naming is inconsistent. The headline claims (300B plateau, 1T/4T optimum) rest on unverified extrapolations in Table 1 and should not be treated as measured results.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
It reports validation of downstream error-rate predictions at 4.5B synthetic tokens, but does not test held-out loss predictions for runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
No architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count are tested.
Tests synthetic-data SFT for mathematical reasoning, with preliminary coding results; does not test other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, or transfer more broadly.
Tests downstream mathematical benchmark performance against synthetic dataset size; does not test performance against pretraining loss or a broad range of downstream tasks.
Compares marginal and rectified scaling forms for one model setting. Does not test compute-optimal allocations, published exponent disagreements, or systematic curve bending.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B
rows.stage_stated: continued training with synthetic data; SFT
rows.operation_detail: Compare fits from the marginal scaling form and the rectified scaling form.
rows.measure: Fit and prediction accuracy of scaling curves
rows.value: The marginal form fails to fit the curve accurately and struggles to predict scaled-up performance; the rectified form captures the curve and predicts effectively.
rows.note: This result shows sensitivity to the fitted functional form in this setting; the comparison does not test compute-optimal splits or exponents across setups.
rows.check: This row also bears on V5: a plain power law in D (Eq. 3) fails to fit or predict the fine-tuning curve, and an extra pre-learned-data term Dl is needed. No fit-error numbers are given; the evidence is Figure 6 and text only.

source_check.correct: The marginal form fails to fit accurately and struggles to predict; the rectified form succeeds after adding Dl. States: V5 partial; V7 observed.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.2, Ablation Study on Scaling Law Form; Figure 6.
source_check.problem: Observed fits V7, but the failure of the unmodified form qualifies V5 rather than demonstrating it fully.
